issues.location: opening countermodel condition for the succedent
issues.finding: The formula metavariable is missing in the quantification over Delta, although the following satisfaction condition contains A.
issues.proposed_resolution: Write A in the quantified succedent formula.

issues.finding: The statement that a failed premise exists for every n is too broad for a finite failure branch ending at an aborted atomic sequent.
issues.proposed_resolution: Apply the successor-premise claim only to stages that have a successor.

issues.location: constant set associated with a failure-branch sequent
issues.finding: The right side is written Delta_n instead of the Lambda_n used for the same branch throughout the definition.
issues.proposed_resolution: Use Lambda_n in the associated sequent.

issues.finding: The conditional begins with a duplicated If.
The right-hand term ends in t_n although the function is m-place and its arguments are t_1 through t_m.
issues.proposed_resolution: Use t_m as the final argument of the interpreted function term.

issues.finding: The tuple has m entries, but the domain power and predicate membership clause use n instead of m.
issues.proposed_resolution: Use m consistently for the domain power and predicate arguments.

issues.location: minimum-index argument in the truth lemma
issues.finding: The proof says the minimum index of the whole successor sequent rises, but older atomic formulas persist with their original lower indices. The algorithm selects the least-indexed non-atomic formula, so the induction argument must refer to that restricted minimum.
issues.proposed_resolution: Qualify each minimum-index claim in the paragraph as the minimum among non-atomic formulas.

issues.location: truth-lemma references to generated premise indices
issues.finding: The displayed conjunction and existential premise descriptions repeat the search algorithm's former k and k+1 indices, despite k being the maximum existing index and newly generated formulas requiring fresh indices above it.
issues.proposed_resolution: Use k+1 and k+2 for two new formulas in one premise and k+1 for a single new formula, matching the corrected search algorithm.
